newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage-backed spreads narrow as Treasuries tank.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage-backed spreads narrow as Treasuries tank.

text.p: Mortgage-backed securities (MBS) spreads were tighter at midday Friday, as Treasuries plunged more than MBS on technical sales and a weaker dollar.
Discount mortgage coupon prices were lower by as much as 12/32 while premium coupons were 2/32 to 3/32 weaker. Treasury 10-year notes, meantime, fell 24/32.
"Accounts appear to be on the sidelines. Most trading seems to be intra-dealer," said a trader.
The plunge in Treasury prices and an ensuing rise in interest rates should support mortgage-backed securities because prepayment concerns were dissipating as rates rose.
"This (rise in Treasury rates) should significantly dampen negative convexity concerns," said Anand Bhattacharya, fixed-income research director at Prudential Securities Inc.
Prepayment concerns were heightened a week ago when the 10-year note yield hovered at 6.0 percent and resulted in some down-in-coupon trades as well as movement into Treasuries.

Participants said that sentiment in Treasuries has since appeared to have changed sharply. Some of the jitters in the Treasury market were tied to fears that July retail sales data due next week might indicate heightened consumer spending.
Nevertherless, holders of mortgage securities were breathing a sigh of relief over the rise in rates experienced in the last five sessions.

"I think there is a major sentiment that we're in a trading range," said one New York market observer. "I don't know where the low point is on the bond. If the market keeps on selling off from here, it will be difficult to say that 6.55 is the low point," he said. The outstanding long bond was yielding 6.65 percent at midday Friday.
Volatilities, the market observer added, may have been up in recent weeks, but were "relatively low compared to year-ago levels. If the market stays at this level, mortgages should do just fine."
Meantime, participants continued to digest Federal National Mortgage Association (FNMA) and Government National Mortgage Association (GNMA) prepayment data released Thursday.

According to Jonathan Raiff of PaineWebber Inc's mortgage strategy group, FNMA prepayments showed faster speeds for all but the highest premium coupons. The 8.5 percent coupon, he said, was the most sensitive to refinancing activity.
The 8.5 percent coupons, Raiff said, "jumped the most with all 8.5s picking up from 12.0 CPR (constant prepayment rate) to 16.2 CPR."
The constant prepayment rate is the percentage of outstanding mortgage loan principal that prepays in one year.
By weighted-average-maturity (WAM), Raiff said, "2027 WAM 8.5s jumped from 21.0 to 31.0 CPR, 2026 WAM 8.5s jumped from 8.5 CPR to 17.4 CPR and 2025 WAM 8.5s jumped from 12.0 to 20.8 CPR."
The weighted average maturity is the average number of months to the final payment of each loan backing a mortgage bond, weighted by the size of the principal loan balances.
PaineWebber's Raiff also saw heightened prepayment activity in 8.0 percent coupons because mortgage rates dipped below 7.5 percent in July.
Eight-percent coupons with a 2027 WAM doubled in speed from 3.9 to 7.8 CPR, while 8.0 percent loans with a 2026 WAM saw CPRs rise to 8.3 from 6.0.

Within the GNMA sector, Raiff reported seeing an increase in prepay speeds of 7.5 percent and 8.0 percent coupons. And "last month, GNMA 8.5s surprised (participants) by jumping from 5 CPR to 16 CPR in the most recent issues," Raiff said, adding that he does not expect more than a further 20 percent rise in GNMA 8.0 or 8.5 percent prepay speeds next month.

Among active 30-year 7.5 percent MBS, GNMAs were off 20/32 at 100-16/32 to yield 7.47 percent, about 107.5 basis points over Treasuries. FNMAs 7.5s were down 19/32 at 100-17/32 and Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp 7.5s were 20/32 lower at 100-23/32.
Ten-year Treasury notes were 1 4/32 weaker on the day at 98 to yield 6.40 percent.
(( --Aleksandrs Rozens, N.A. Mortgage Unit, 212-859-1668 ))
